questions.question: The clavicle articulates medially with the:
questions.explanation: Laterally it articulates with the acromion of the scapula.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The spine of the scapula divides the dorsal surface into the:
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus lies in the former and infraspinatus in the latter.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The surgical neck of the humerus is closely related to the:

options.C: Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery

questions.explanation: Radial nerve lies in the spiral groove of the shaft.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pectoralis major is supplied by:
questions.explanation: It adducts and medially rotates the arm.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The nerve to latissimus dorsi is the:
questions.explanation: From the posterior cord of the brachial plexus (C6–C8).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The axillary artery is divided into three parts by the:
questions.explanation: It continues as the brachial artery at the lower border of teres major.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The brachial artery bifurcates into radial and ulnar arteries at the level of the:

options.A: Neck of the radius in the cubital fossa

questions.explanation: The pulse is felt medial to the biceps tendon.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The cephalic vein drains into the:
questions.explanation: The basilic vein joins the brachial veins to form the axillary vein.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Flexor digitorum profundus has a dual nerve supply: the lateral half by the:

options.C: Anterior interosseous nerve (median) and the medial half by the ulnar nerve

questions.explanation: Allows FDP to act on the DIP joints.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The first dorsal compartment of the wrist contains the tendons of:

options.B: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis

questions.explanation: Inflamed in De Quervain's tenosynovitis.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which muscle is NOT a thenar muscle?
questions.explanation: Adductor pollicis is ulnar nerve supplied; the others are mostly median.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The median nerve passes between the two heads of:
questions.explanation: Entrapment causes pronator syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The posterior interosseous nerve passes through the:
questions.explanation: A deep branch of the radial nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The three bones that fuse to form the hip bone are:
questions.explanation: They meet in the acetabulum.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The acetabular labrum functions to:

options.C: Deepen the socket and increase hip stability

questions.explanation: Tears cause hip pain and impingement.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The strongest ligament of the human body is the:
questions.explanation: It prevents hyperextension of the hip.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The long head of biceps femoris is supplied by the:

options.D: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve

questions.explanation: The short head is supplied by the common peroneal division.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The sartorius muscle is supplied by the:
questions.explanation: It flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip (tailor's position).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The adductor magnus has a dual nerve supply from the obturator nerve and the:

options.A: Tibial part of the sciatic nerve

questions.explanation: Its hamstring part acts as a hip extensor.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The safe site for intragluteal injection is the:

options.B: Upper outer quadrant of the buttock

questions.explanation: Avoids the sciatic nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most superficial structure in the popliteal fossa is the:
questions.explanation: From superficial to deep: nerve, vein, artery.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Tibialis anterior is supplied by the:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The peroneal (fibular) muscles evert the foot and are supplied by the:
questions.explanation: Peroneus tertius is supplied by the deep peroneal nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The deep posterior compartment of the leg contains:

options.D: Tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus

questions.explanation: Mnemonic: Tom, Dick and Harry (from medial to lateral).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The skin and intrinsic muscles of the sole are supplied by the:

options.D: Medial and lateral plantar nerves (branches of the tibial nerve)

questions.explanation: Medial plantar is the ‘median nerve of the foot’.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The number of tarsal bones is:
questions.explanation: Calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid and three cuneiforms.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The tibialis posterior tendon mainly inserts on the:
questions.explanation: Also slips to all tarsals except talus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The saphenous nerve is a branch of the:
questions.explanation: It supplies the medial side of the leg and foot.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The linea alba is formed by the fusion of the:

options.C: Aponeuroses of the abdominal wall muscles in the midline

questions.explanation: A common site for hernias.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The inguinal canal in the male transmits the:
questions.explanation: In the female the round ligament.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which organ is retroperitoneal?
questions.explanation: Others: pancreas (mostly), duodenum (2nd–4th parts), aorta.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Oxygenated blood from the lungs enters the heart at the:
questions.explanation: Via four pulmonary veins.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The SA node is supplied by the right coronary artery in about:
questions.explanation: In the rest from the left circumflex artery.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The trachea bifurcates at the level of the:
questions.explanation: Foreign bodies enter the right bronchus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: How many pairs of cranial nerves are there?
questions.explanation: Spinal nerves: 31 pairs.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The three divisions of the trigeminal nerve are:
questions.explanation: V1 and V2 are purely sensory; V3 has motor fibres.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The nerve with the most extensive distribution in the thorax and abdomen is the:
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic supply to the heart and gut.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Injury to the hypoglossal nerve causes the tongue to deviate:

options.D: Toward the side of the lesion

questions.explanation: Genioglossus pushes the tongue forward on the intact side.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The thalamus acts as the relay station for all sensory pathways EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Olfactory pathways reach the cortex directly.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The hippocampus is important for:
questions.explanation: Bilateral damage causes anterograde amnesia.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The lateral spinothalamic tract carries:
questions.explanation: Fibres decussate near the level of entry.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Corticospinal fibres pass through the:

options.A: Posterior limb of the internal capsule

questions.explanation: A small infarct here causes hemiplegia.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The ascending reticular activating system is important for:
questions.explanation: Damage causes coma.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: CSF is produced mainly by the:
questions.explanation: Reabsorbed by arachnoid villi into the venous sinuses.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy; Gray's Anatomy for Students (chapter-level reference)
